clue.text: It can change an old buffoon

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A remark that something can transform a clown from days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IT CAN gives the letters; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As an archaic noun the word meant a grotesque performer or clown, hence 'old'.

clue.text: A quiet attendant about to put a stop to a hanger-on

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the attendant word goes round the stopping word

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant
to end something is to put a stop to it

explanation.surface: A silent servant is about to finish off a parasitic follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is a thing attached to something bigger, literally something that hangs on.

clue.text: Grows weary, but tries anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any haphazard order, so the letters of the word tries are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flags yet keeps trying regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: To tire is to become fatigued, so the third-person form matches the clue verb.

clue.text: Thousands have to drive around in traffic

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the first piece holds the second
around says the forcing word goes round the outside of the numbers

parts.note: to coerce is to force or drive someone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Thousands of people are forced to drive round and round in heavy traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' looks like cars on a road, but it means trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in its older sense is buying and selling goods, which is what commerce means.

clue.text: Stiffening, bend over in pain

indicators.note: in places the bending word inside the pain word

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
to arch is to bend over in a curve

explanation.surface: Someone stiffens up, doubled over in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is applied to fabric to make it rigid, so applying it is stiffening.

clue.text: Hit the drink!

definitions.meaning: a mouthful of spirits, a swig

explanation.surface: An order to start boozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the drink' sounds like an urging to start drinking; split it into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a heavy punch and a gulp of liquor.

clue.text: Starry-eyed forecaster

parts.note: starry-eyed usually means naive, but here it is one whose eyes are on the stars to predict the future

explanation.definitionFit: Horoscope writers predict events by watching the positions of stars and planets.

clue.text: The artist's surrounded by pets — they're worth their weight in gold

definitions.text: they're worth their weight in gold

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the artist inside the pets word

parts.note: cats are household pets
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter among his animals, who are precious companions.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'worth their weight in gold' means invaluable; read literally, these units do measure the fineness of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a unit of gold purity, twenty-four parts making pure gold, so value in gold is reckoned in them.

clue.text: The fashionable form? Quite the reverse!

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a version is a form or variant of something

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is the trendy shape, then retorting that it is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning something the other way round, the exact opposite, is a reversal or upending.

clue.text: A common plant in Hong Kong or Seoul

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the run of place names that follows

explanation.surface: A weed found growing in two big Asian cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Kong or Seoul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny yellow-flowered furze grows wild on heaths and commons.

clue.text: Average lot, yet outstanding

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a lot is a quantity or amount

explanation.surface: Something ordinary in quantity that is nevertheless superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, chief, standing above all others.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader remaining a wanderer

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Revolutionary

parts.note: over means left over, remaining

explanation.surface: The head of a rebellion is still a nomad.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is someone who roams from place to place.

clue.text: Made a home for a good man in straitened circumstances

indicators.note: in puts the saint inside the poverty word

parts.note: need is poverty, straitened circumstances
ST, saint, is the crossword stock for a good man

explanation.surface: Someone housed a virtuous man who had fallen on hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that build a nest and settle there have set up home.

clue.text: Situation vacant — write without obligation

parts.note: a post is a job, a situation
free means unoccupied, vacant

explanation.surface: A job advertisement inviting written applications with nothing binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Situation vacant' reads as a jobs heading; 'write' is the link of the advert's 'write in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent post-free means postage is paid, so the recipient bears no charge or commitment.

clue.text: I dn, very old and in a hole

definitions.text: very old and in a hole

parts.words: I dn, very old and in a hole
parts.note: unreadable: the scan garbled the clue's opening words, so they cannot be explained; surface reading: someone ancient who has fallen on hard times; setter's reading: the hole is a cave, where an ancient limestone formation hangs from the roof

explanation.walkthrough: The scanned clue's opening is corrupted, so only its readable tail is explained here; that part describes the answer without separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: These icicle-shaped mineral deposits take thousands of years to grow, dripping down from cave ceilings underground.

clue.text: Regal resignation

parts.note: a monarch's stepping down from the throne

explanation.definitionFit: Giving up the crown is the royal form of quitting, as Edward VIII did in 1936.

clue.text: Game people going under upset no-one

parts.note: divers go under water

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman one

explanation.surface: A sporting crowd sinking under a disappointment that bothered nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but reverses NOI to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a pastime or amusement, as a game is.

clue.text: Wooden Greek character given quarters

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
N and E, north and east, are compass quarters

explanation.surface: A stiff Greek figure is offered lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' suggests stiff acting; here it describes timber, as in pine furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine used attributively describes things made of that softwood timber.

clue.text: 16 is always concerned about the environment

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
green means environmentally minded

explanation.surface: The tree in 16 is ever the eco-conscious one.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is PINE, a tree that keeps its needles all year.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer keeping its leaves through winter is an example of a tree never bare.

clue.text: A number of bonds are for a ten-year period

parts.note: nine is a number
ties bind things together

explanation.surface: Financial bonds issued with a ten-year term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonds' suggests investments; it means things that tie.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineties are a decade, such as the years 1990 to 1999, spanning exactly a tenth of a century.

clue.text: Feel jealous of a minister who lacks nothing

indicators.note: who lacks tells us the diplomat is missing the zero

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic minister
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: Resenting a diplomat who has no possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: To envy is to begrudge another their good fortune.

clue.text: Loyalty to a certain party for instance admitted by a union

indicators.note: admitted by puts the example abbreviation inside the union word

parts.note: an alliance is a union of parties
EG, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: Political fidelity shown, say, by members of a coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithful commitment owed to a sovereign, cause or side.

clue.text: A country road circumventing a regulation

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the road letters surround the rest

parts.note: MI is the crossword form of the M1, Britain's first motorway
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: A rural lane bypassing a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A country road' looks like one phrase; 'A country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Acidity a medico can dry out

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: out signals the letters of can dry are put out of order

explanation.surface: Sharpness of tongue that a doctor can drain away.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordancy is biting sharpness, of a substance or of a remark.

clue.text: Mirror showing Bohemian girl with large figure

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
C, a hundred, is a large Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A looking-glass reflecting a bohemian girl with a full figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror someone is to copy their movements exactly, which is what an impersonator does.

clue.text: Jack's water-spaniel?

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor; his hound of the waves, playfully, would be an old salt

explanation.definitionFit: An old sailor is called this, and the phrase read literally is a dog of the ocean.

clue.text: This is an Elizabethan bowler, duck!

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ... is said to have finished his game of bowls on Plymouth Hoe before fighting the Armada

explanation.surface: A shout warning someone to dodge a Tudor-era sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' reads as a warning to get down; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Elizabethan sea captain and lawn-bowls player, the other the male mallard.

clue.text: Catch up a bit

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to trap is to catch

explanation.surface: An invitation to make up some lost ground slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A part is a portion or piece of something.

clue.text: A woman's fate

definitions.meaning: in Greek thought ... is a person's allotted destiny

explanation.surface: What life holds in store for a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a female first name, the other the Greek word for destiny.

clue.text: Totally without vitality for a time — in an awful state

indicators.note: being in an awful state means being in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone completely drained for a while and in a terrible condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in an awful state' reads as one phrase, but 'in an' is part of the anagram with 'a time'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, wholly lacking spirit or life.

clue.text: Temperate land mass

definitions.meaning: one of the earth's great land areas

explanation.surface: A region of the globe with a mild climate.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means exercising self-control; the noun names a vast landmass such as Asia.

clue.text: Back authoritarian

explanation.surface: Supporting a strict ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the after part of a vessel, the other a harsh, unbending manner.
